name: FronTalk
intro: FronTalk是一个多轮、多模态前端代码生成基准。论文从C4抽样10,000个网页，经GPT-4o摘要、BERTopic聚类与人工选择得到100个网站，再生成并人工精炼10轮功能/设计意图及测试。最终100个对话含1,000轮和3,676个测试用例，文本与视觉模拟器表达等价意图，并通过网页智能体评估指令遵循、遗忘和可用性。
build_method: C4网页抽样与BERTopic聚类, 人工选择100站, GPT-4o生成十轮意图与测试, 人工删除/编辑问题用例, 双用户模拟器
modality: 文本, 图像, 代码
task_type: 前端代码生成, 多轮软件工程
eval_feature: 多模态反馈, 智能体评估, 遗忘分析
intro_en: FronTalk is a multi-turn, multimodal front-end code-generation benchmark. The paper samples 10,000 C4 webpages, uses GPT-4o summaries, BERTopic clustering, and manual selection to obtain 100 sites, then generates and manually refines ten turns of functional/design intents and tests. The final 100 dialogues contain 1,000 turns and 3,676 test cases; textual and visual simulators express equivalent intents, and web agents assess instruction following, forgetting, and usability.
build_method_en: C4 Web Sampling and BERTopic Clustering, Manual 100-site Selection, GPT-4o Ten-turn Intent/Test Generation, Manual Removal/Editing, Dual User Simulators
task_type_en: Front-end Code Generation, Multi-turn Software Engineering
eval_feature_en: Multimodal Feedback, Agent-based Evaluation, Forgetting Analysis

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2601.04203v2 §2.1-§2.4, §3.2, Appendix D, Appendix E, and Appendix I, plus official repository snapshot 4486cf0. FronTalk samples 10,000 C4 pages, summarizes with GPT-4o, clusters with BERTopic, and manually chooses 100 representatives. GPT-4o randomly selects functional/design intent type for each of ten turns. All tests are manually refined: 66 removed, 2,783 edited, and an independent 224-case sample rises from 90.1% to 94.7% validity; the initial refiner number and qualifications are not disclosed. Text simulation uses current code plus original intent to resolve ambiguity/redundancy; simulator validation covers 114 instructions/411 tests. Primary evaluation scores all intents/tests on the final output and naive first-time-user UX against curated references. Equation (2) aggregates the first T-1 turns: FR = 1 - sum_{t<T} PC(o_T|i_t) / sum_{t<T} PC(o_t|i_t), so final-output retention is the numerator and original-turn passing is the denominator. Separate human checks cover 218 pass cases and 50 UX pairs.
